name: Lisa Frank
blurb: Rainbow-neon stickers, folders and Trapper Keepers with unicorns, pandas and dolphins
title: Lisa Frank: The 90s Sticker and School Supply Brand, Then and Now
description: Lisa Frank's rainbow animal art covered stickers, folders and Trapper Keepers in the 1980s–90s. The company shrank in the 2000s and now licenses its designs.
answer: Lisa Frank is an American design company, founded around 1980 in Tucson, Arizona, whose neon, rainbow-colored pictures of unicorns, pandas, dolphins and other animals covered stickers, folders, Trapper Keepers and lunchboxes in the 1980s and 1990s. At its 1990s peak it reported more than $60 million a year in sales. Sales fell sharply in the 2000s, but the brand never closed and is still licensed for collaborations, helped by a 2024 Prime Video docuseries and a wave of 1990s nostalgia.

sections.h: What Lisa Frank stuff looked like
body: The look is instantly recognisable: saturated rainbow and neon colors and stylised, wide-eyed animals such as unicorns, pandas and dolphins. Until 1989 the designs were airbrushed by hand, each taking anywhere from nine to 36 hours, before the company moved to computer software.

The company began with stickers, and Spencer Gifts placed its first million-dollar order. From 1987 the same art went onto school supplies, which is where most people met it: folders, notebooks, pencil cases, erasers, lunchboxes and Trapper Keeper binders, popular above all with elementary and middle school girls. The slogan, from the late 1980s, was "You Gotta Have It".

head: Year
What happened
rows: Lisa Frank Inc. grows out of a small children's jewelry business in Tucson and starts making stickers
Sales take off with school supplies in the company's designs
Annual sales above $60 million at the peak
Sales fall and staff at the headquarters shrink from a peak of about 500 to six; revenue in 2012 is estimated at $2.3 million
Urban Outfitters sells vintage Lisa Frank merchandise as nostalgia picks up
Licensed collaborations: Reebok shoes (2017), a Morphe eyeshadow palette (2020), Pillsbury unicorn cookie dough (2021), Crocs (2023)
Prime Video releases the four-part docuseries Glitter and Greed: The Lisa Frank Story on December 5

body: By the 2000s the products were much harder to find in stores, the company's own retail shops had closed, and it made little new stationery. Rather than disappearing, the brand turned into an archive of artwork that other companies license for limited editions, from clothing to make-up and shoes, while its Instagram following grew in the early 2020s.
The 2024 docuseries looked at how the brand rose and seemed to vanish, and included former employees describing a demanding and difficult workplace. The company is still based in Tucson.

sections.h: Can you still get it, and is it worth anything?
body: New Lisa Frank designs appear mostly through licensed collaborations sold for a limited time. Original 1980s and 1990s folders, stickers and Trapper Keepers are now second-hand and collector items. Most used pieces are worth little; condition matters a great deal, and only rare items in unused condition draw serious collector interest. There is no official price guide.

faq.q: Is Lisa Frank a real person?
faq.a: Yes. Lisa Frank is the American artist and businesswoman who founded the company and whose name is on the products.

faq.q: Is Lisa Frank still in business?
faq.a: Yes. The company is smaller than in the 1990s, but it still exists in Tucson and licenses its designs for new products.
A four-part Prime Video documentary series, released in December 2024, about the rise and fall of Lisa Frank Inc.
